text:
The minimum number of times one has to toss a
fair coin so that the probability of observing at least
one head is at least 90% is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Probablity of getting head P(H) = $\frac{1}{2}$

Probablity of getting tail P(T) = 1 - $\frac{1}{2}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$

Probability of observing at least one head out of n tosses

= 1 - Probability of observing no head occurs out of n tosses

= 1 - $\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{n}$

According to the question,

1 - $\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{n}$ $\geq$ $\frac{90}{100}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{n}\leq \frac{1}{10}$

$\Rightarrow$ $2^{n}\geq 10$

As $2^{3} = 8$

$2^{4} = 16$

$\therefore$ Minimum value of n = 4
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
Let $\vec{a}=3i^{\wedge }+2j^{\wedge }+xk^{\wedge }$ and $\vec{b}=i^{\wedge }-j^{\wedge }+k^{\wedge }$
, for some real x. Then $\left |\vec{a}\times \vec{b}\right |$ = r
 is possible if :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{a}\times \vec{b}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 3 & 2 & x \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{array}\right |$

= (2 + x)$\hat{i}$ + (3 - x)$\hat{j}$ - 5$\widehat{k}$

$\left |\vec{a}\times \vec{b}\right |$ = r

= $\sqrt{(2+x)^{2}+(x-3)^{2}+(-5)^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ r = $\sqrt{4+4x+x^{2}+x^{2}+9-6x+25}$

= $\sqrt{2x^{2}-2x+38}$

= $\sqrt{2\left (x^{2}-x+\frac{1}{4}\right )+38-\frac{1}{2}}$

= $\sqrt{2\left (x-\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}+\frac{75}{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$  r $\geq$ $\sqrt{\frac{75}{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $r\geq 5\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
If the fourth term in the binomial expansion of

$\left (\sqrt{x^{\left (\frac{1}{1+\log 10x}\right )}}+x^{\frac{1}{12}}\right )^{6}$  is equal to 200, and x > 1,
then the value of x is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Fourth term $(T_{4})$

= ${}^{6}C_{3}\left (\sqrt{x^{\left (\frac{1}{1+\log 10x}\right )}}\right )^{3}\left (x^{\frac{1}{12}}\right )^{3}$

= $20\left (x^{\left (\frac{1}{1+\log 10x}\right )}\right )^{\frac{3}{2}}\left (x^{\frac{1}{4}}\right )$

= $20\times x^{\left (\frac{1}{1+\log 10x}\right )\frac{3}{2}}\times x^{\frac{1}{4}}$

= $20\times x^{\left (\frac{3}{2\left (1+\log 10x\right )}+\frac{1}{4}\right )}$

Given, $T_{4} = 200$

$\therefore$ $20\times x^{\left (\frac{3}{2\left (1+\log 10x\right )}+\frac{1}{4}\right )}$ = 200

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{\left (\frac{3}{2\left (1+\log 10x\right )}+\frac{1}{4}\right )}$ = 10

Taking $\log _{10}$ on both sides

$\left (\frac{3}{2(1+\log _{10}x)}+\frac{1}{4}\right )\log _{10}x$ = 1

put $\log _{10} x = t$

$\left (\frac{3}{2(1+t)}+\frac{1}{4}\right )t$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{(1+t)+6}{4(1+t)}\right )\times t$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $t^{2} + 7t = 4 + 4t$

$\Rightarrow$ $t^{2} + 3t - 4 = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ (t + 4)(t - 1) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ t = 1 or t = - 4

$\therefore$ $\log _{10} x = 1$

$\Rightarrow$ x = 10

or $\log _{10} x = - 4$

$\Rightarrow$ $x = 10^{-4}$

But as x > 1 so x $\neq$ $10^{-4}$

$\therefore$ x = 10
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
Let ƒ : R $\to$ R be a differentiable function
satisfying ƒ'(3) + ƒ'(2) = 0.

Then $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{1+f(3+x)-f(3)}{1+f(2-x)-f(2)}\right )^{\frac{1}{x}}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The general formula for indeterminate form $1^{$\infty} is

$\lim _{x\to a}(f(x))^{g(x)}=e^{\lim _{x\to a}g(x)(f(x)-1)}$

I = $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{1+f(3+x)-f(3)}{1+f(2-x)-f(2)}\right )^{\frac{1}{x}}$

Here I is in $1^{$\infty} form.

$\therefore$ I = $e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{1+f(3+x)-f(3)}{1+f(2-x)-f(2)}-1\right )\frac{1}{x}}$

= $e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{1+f(3+x)-f(3)-1-f(2-x)+f(2)}{1+f(2-x)-f(2)}\right )\frac{1}{x}}$

= $e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{f(3+x)-f(3)-f(2-x)+f(2)}{1+f(2-x)-f(2)}\right )\frac{1}{x}}$

Here $\frac{f(3+x)-f(3)-f(2-x)+f(2)}{x}$ is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form.

So using L'Hopital rule we get

= $e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{f'(3+x)+f'(2-x)}{1}\right ).\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{1}{1+f(2-x)-f(2)}\right )}$

= $e^{(f^{'}(3)+f^{'}(2)).1}$

$= e^{0}$  [ as given ƒ'(3) + ƒ'(2) = 0 ]

= 1

text:
Let the number 2,b,c be in an A.P. and

A = $\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & b & c \\ 4 & b^{2} & c^{2} \end{array}\right ]$. If det(A) $\in$ [2, 16], then c
lies in the interval :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
2, b, c are in AP.

Let common difference = d

$\therefore$ b = 2 + d and c = 2 + 2d

|A| = $\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & b & c \\ 4 & b^{2} & c^{2} \end{array}\right ]$

$C_{2} = C_{2} - C_{1}$

$C_{3} = C_{3} - C_{1}$

= $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & b-2 & c-2 \\ 4 & b^{2}-4 & c^{2}-4 \end{array}\right |$

= $(b-2)(c-2)\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & b+2 & c+2 \end{array}\right |$

= $(b-2)(c-2)[c+2-b-2]$

= $(b-2)(c-2)(c-b)$

[ As b = 2 + d and c = 2 + 2d, then b - 2 = 4, c - 2 = 2d and c - b = d]

= (d) (2d) (d)

$= 2d^{3}$

Given |A| $\in$ [2, 16]

$\therefore$ $2d^{3}$ $\in$ [2, 16]

$\Rightarrow$ $d^{3}$ $\in$ [1, 8]

$\Rightarrow$ d $\in$ [1, 2]

As c = 2 + 2d

then c $\in$ [4, 6]
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
If three distinct numbers a, b, c are in G.P. and the
equations $ax^{2}$
 + 2bx + c = 0 and
$dx^{2}$
 + 2ex + ƒ = 0 have a common root, then
which one of the following statements is
correct?
options: d, e, ƒ are in A.P
d, e, ƒ are in G.P
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, a, b, c are in G.P.

$\therefore$ $b^{2} = ac$

In this equation $ax^{2}$
 + 2bx + c = 0,

Discrimant, $D = 4b^{2} - 4ac$

= 4ac - 4ac

= 0

Discrimant = 0 meand roots of the equation are equal.

Let both the roots of the equation = $α$

$\therefore$ 2$α$ = $-\frac{2b}{a}$

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = $-\frac{b}{a}$

As both the
equations $ax^{2}$
 + 2bx + c = 0 and
$dx^{2}$
 + 2ex + ƒ = 0 have a common root,

so $-\frac{b}{a}$ is also root of the equation $dx^{2}$
 + 2ex + ƒ = 0.

$\therefore$ $-\frac{b}{a}$ satisfy the equation $dx^{2}$
 + 2ex + ƒ = 0.

$\therefore$ $d\left (-\frac{b}{a}\right )^{2}+2e\left (-\frac{b}{a}\right )+f=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $db^{2}-2aeb+fa^{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $dac-2aeb+fa^{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $dc-2eb+fa=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dc}{ac}-\frac{2eb}{ac}+\frac{fa}{ac}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dc}{ac}-\frac{2eb}{b^{2}}+\frac{fa}{ac}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{d}{a}-\frac{2e}{b}+\frac{f}{c}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2e}{b}=\frac{d}{a}+\frac{f}{c}$

$\therefore$ 
$\frac{d}{a}$, $\frac{e}{b}$, $\frac{f}{c}$ are in A.P.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
Let $f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}g(t)dt$  where g is a non-zero even
function. If ƒ(x + 5) = g(x), then $\int\limits _{0}^{x}f(t)dt$ equals-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}g(t)dt$

$f(-x)=\int\limits _{0}^{-x}g(t)dt$

Put t = -v

= $-\int\limits _{0}^{x}g(-v)dv$ 

= $-\int\limits _{0}^{x}g(v)d(v)$ [ as g(v) is an even function.]

= - f(x)

$\Rightarrow$ f(-x) = -f(x)

$\therefore$  f(x) is an odd function.

Given ƒ(x + 5) = g(x)

$\therefore$ g(- x) = ƒ(- x + 5) 

$\Rightarrow$ g(x) = - f(x - 5) [as g(x) is even and f(x) is an odd function]

Replacing x by x + 5, we get

f(x) = - g(x + 5) ......(1)

Now

$\int\limits _{0}^{x}f(t)dt$

= $-\int\limits _{0}^{x}g(t+5)dt$

= $-\int\limits _{5}^{x+5}g(t)dt$

= $\int\limits _{x+5}^{5}g(t)dt$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
In an ellipse, with centre at the origin, if the
difference of the lengths of major axis and minor
axis is 10 and one of the foci is at (0,5$\sqrt{3}$), then
the length of its latus rectum is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Focus (0, be) = (0, 5$\sqrt{3}$)

$\therefore$ be = 5$\sqrt{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $b^{2}e^{2} = 75$

As here b > a

so $e^{2} =$ $1-\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}$

$\therefore$ $b^{2}\left (1-\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}\right )$ = 75

$\Rightarrow$ $b^{2} - a^{2} = 75 .......(1)$

Given that,

difference of the lengths of major axis and minor
axis is 10.

$\therefore$ 2b - 2a = 10

$\Rightarrow$ b - a = 5 .......(2)

From (1),

(b + a)(b - a) = 75

$\Rightarrow$ (b + a)5 = 75

$\Rightarrow$ (b + a) = 15 .......(3)

From (2) and (3) we get,

b = 10, a = 5

$\therefore$ Length of its latus rectum = $\frac{2a^{2}}{b}$

= $\frac{2\times 25}{10}$ = 5
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
If ƒ(1) = 1, ƒ'(1) = 3, then the derivative of
ƒ(ƒ(ƒ(x))) + (ƒ$(x))^{2}$ at x = 1 is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given ƒ(1) = 1, ƒ'(1) = 3

Let y = ƒ(ƒ(ƒ(x))) + (ƒ$(x))^{2}$

On differentiating both sides with respect to x we get,

$\frac{dy}{dx}$ = ƒ'(ƒ(ƒ(x))).ƒ'(ƒ(x)).ƒ'(x) + 2ƒ(x).ƒ'(x)

Now at x = 1,

$\frac{dy}{dx}$ = ƒ'(ƒ(ƒ(1))).ƒ'(ƒ(1)).ƒ'(1) + 2ƒ(1).ƒ'(1)

= ƒ'(ƒ(1)).ƒ'(1).ƒ'(1) + 2.1.ƒ'(1)

= ƒ'(1).ƒ'(1).ƒ'(1) + 2.1.ƒ'(1)

= 3$\times$3$\times$3 + 2$\times$3

= 33

text:
If $\int \frac{dx}{x^{3}(1+x^{6})^{2/3}}=xf(x)(1+x^{6})^{\frac{1}{3}}+C$ 

where C is a constant of integration, then the
function ƒ(x) is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
I = $\int \frac{dx}{x^{3}(1+x^{6})^{\dfrac{2}{3}}}$

= $\int \frac{dx}{x^{7}\left (\frac{1}{x6}+1\right )^{\dfrac{2}{3}}}$

Let $\frac{1}{x^{6}}+1$ = t

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{-6}{x^{7}}dx=dt$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dx}{x^{7}}=-\frac{dt}{6}$

$\therefore$ I = $-\frac{1}{6}\int \frac{dt}{t^{\dfrac{2}{3}}}$

= $-\frac{1}{6}\left [\frac{t^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}{\frac{1}{3}}\right ]+C$

= $-\frac{1}{2}\left [\frac{1}{x^{6}}+1\right ]^{\frac{1}{3}}+C$

= $-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\left (1+x^{6}\right )^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}{x^{2}}\times \frac{x}{x}+C$

= $x.\left (-\frac{1}{2x^{3}}\right ).\left (1+x^{6}\right )^{\frac{1}{3}}+C$

$\therefore$ f(x) = $-\frac{1}{2x^{3}}$

text:
Suppose that the points (h,k), (1,2) and (–3,4) lie
on the line $L_{1}$
. If a line $L_{2}$
 passing through the points
(h,k) and (4,3) is perpendicular to $L_{1}$
, then
$\frac{k}{h}$
equals :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Equation of line $L_{1}$ passing through points (1, 2) and (–3, 4) is :

y - 2 = $\left (\frac{4-2}{-3-1}\right )$(x - 1)

$\Rightarrow$ y - 2 = $-\frac{1}{2}$(x - 1)

$\Rightarrow$ 2y – 4 = –x + 1

$\Rightarrow$ $x + 2y = 5 .......(L_{1})$

Line $L_{1}$ passes through point (h, k).

$\therefore$ h + 2k = 5 .......(1)

Line $L_{2}$ is perpendicular to line $L_{1}$.

$\therefore$ Equation of line $L_{2}$ :

2x - y = $λ$

This line $L_{2}$ passes through point (4, 3).

$\therefore$ 2(4) - 3 = $λ$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = 5

$\therefore$ Line $L_{2}$ :

2x - y = 5

$L_{2}$ also passes through (h, k)

$\therefore$ 2h - k = 5  ............(2)

Solving (1) and (2) we get,

h = 3 and k = 1

$\therefore$ $\frac{k}{h}=\frac{1}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

Let ƒ : [–1,3] $\to$ R be defined as

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{lll} |x|+[x] & , & -1\leq x<1 \\ x+|x| & , & 1\leq x<2 \\ x+[x] & , & 2\leq x\leq 3 \end{array} \right.$

where [t] denotes the greatest integer less than
or equal to t. Then, ƒ is discontinuous at:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{lll} |x|+[x] & , & -1\leq x<1 \\ x+|x| & , & 1\leq x<2 \\ x+[x] & , & 2\leq x\leq 3 \end{array} \right.$

= $=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} -x-1, & -1\leq x<0 \\ x, & 0\leq x<1 \\ 2x, & 1\leq x<2 \\ x+2, & 2\leq x<3 \\ 6, & x=3 \end{array} \right.$

f(-1) = $\lim _{x\to -1}(-x-1)$ =  -( -1) - 1 = 0

$f(-1^{+}) =$ $\lim _{x\to -1^{+}}(-x-1)$ = 0

$\therefore$ f(x) is continuous at x = - 1

$f(0^{-}) =\lim _{x\to 0^{-}}(-x-1)$

 =  -(0) - 1 = - 1

f(0) = $\lim _{x\to 0}(x)$ = 0

$f(0^{+}) =$ $\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}(x)$ = 0

$\therefore$ f(x) is discontinuous at x = 0

$f(1^{-}) =$ $\lim _{x\to 1^{-}}(x)$ = 1

f(1) = $\lim _{x\to 1}(2x)$ = 2

$f(1^{+}) =$ $\lim _{x\to 1^{+}}(2x)$ = 2

$\therefore$ f(x) is discontinuous at x = 1

$f(3^{-}) =$ $\lim _{x\to 3^{-}}(x+2)$ = 3 + 2 = 5

f(3) = 6

$\therefore$ f(x) is discontinuous at x = 3

So, f(x) is discontinuous at x = {0, 1, 3}.

text:
The number of four-digit numbers strictly greater
than 4321 that can be formed using the digits
0,1,2,3,4,5 (repetition of digits is allowed) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A four-digit number greater than 4321 formed from 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 must begin with 4 or 5.

First digit 5: each of the other three places takes any of the 6 digits, giving $6^{3}=216$ numbers.

First digit 4 and second digit 4 or 5: $2\times 6\times 6=72$ numbers.

First two digits 4, 3 and third digit 3, 4 or 5: $3\times 6=18$ numbers.

First three digits 4, 3, 2 and last digit 2, 3, 4 or 5: $4$ numbers. A smaller second or third digit gives a number below 4321.

Total $=216+72+18+4=310$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Here r = 3 cos$θ$

and $\frac{h}{2}$ = 3 sin$θ$

$\Rightarrow$ h = 6 sin$θ$

We know, Volume of cylinder

V = $π$ $r^{2} h$

$\Rightarrow$ V = $π$ $(9\cos ^{2}θ$)(6 sin$θ$)

$\Rightarrow$ V = 54$π$ (sin$θ$ $- \sin ^{3}θ$)

For maxima/minima of volume,

$\frac{dV}{dθ}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ cos$θ$ $- 3\sin ^{2}θ$ cos$θ$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ cos$θ(1 - 3\sin ^{2}θ$) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ cos$θ$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $θ$ = $\frac{π}{2}$ (not possible)

or $1 - 3\sin ^{2}θ$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ sin$θ$ = $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$\therefore$ h = 6 sin$θ$ = $\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}}$ = $2\sqrt{3}$
